claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 19 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you a few questions about Alex to determine his eligibility.

Since Alex is 19, an important factor is whether he's in approved education or training. Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A few more questions about Alex:

Is Alex working at all? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's just focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good to know. Now I need to ask about your living situation:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure actually - my living situation is a bit complicated at the moment and I'm not certain about my residency status.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that living situations can be complicated. Let me ask a bit more to understand your circumstances better.

Are you currently physically living in the UK right now, even if you're uncertain about your residency status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Look, I'm really not certain about the details. My situation is unclear and I can't give you a definite answer about whether I'm in the UK or not right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - thank you for being honest about your uncertainty regarding your location and living situation.

Let me also ask: Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him, or are you contributing financially to his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me - he's at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you.

Just to clarify one more thing: When you say Alex lives "at home with me," are you able to confirm whether that home is located in the UK, or is this part of the uncertainty you mentioned about your living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's part of what I'm uncertain about - I really can't say for sure whether we're in the UK or not. It's just not clear at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, thank you for clarifying. Let me ask a few more questions to complete my assessment:

1. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

2. Has Alex started receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him - it's just me looking after him. And no, he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask one final question:

Is Alex in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just at home with me.
